headline: AGNICO EAGLE AND ALAMOS GOLD REPORT TONIGHT — Street Sees $3.51B Revenue for AEM; Gold Sector on Edge After 35% Q4 Selloff
snippet: Agnico Eagle (AEM) and Alamos Gold (AGI) both report Q3 2026 results after market close today, with the Street expecting $3.51 billion in revenue and $2.44 EPS from Agnico — the quarter's results arrive with the sector trading 30-40% below its 2026 highs and fund managers watching cost inflation closely. Alamos consensus sits at $0.44 EPS on $543 million revenue; the earnings call is October 29 at 10 AM ET for Alamos and 11 AM ET for Agnico.

headline: AUSTRALIA REWRITES CRITICAL MINERALS STRATEGY: Government Backs Domestic Refining; Arafura Nolans Targeted as Template
snippet: Resources Minister Madeleine King unveiled a revised Australian critical minerals strategy today that shifts emphasis from raw exports to domestic processing and refining, backed by a new Strategic Reserve and expanded government financing — with Arafura Rare Earths' Nolans project cited as the template for ore-to-oxide integrated production. The policy change arrives with ASX rare earth miners rallying on the news, as the government commits to purchasing up to 500 tonnes of REEs annually from Nolans for five years under the Strategic Reserve.

headline: AI DATA CENTERS TRIGGER STRUCTURAL URANIUM SUPPLY DEFICIT — Nuclear the Only 24/7 Grid-Scale Option; Mine Supply Cannot Keep Pace
snippet: A new analysis argues that AI data-centre power demand has shifted nuclear energy from a niche baseload option to a strategic necessity, creating a structural uranium supply deficit that conventional mine pipelines cannot address within a 10-year horizon. Uranium spot is near $89.63/lb with long-term contracts at $96.50 — above the 2007 cycle peak — while reactor build-out is accelerating faster than any comparable prior cycle.

headline: 93% OF U.S. REACTOR URANIUM CAME FROM OVERSEAS IN 2025 — EIA Data Flags Structural Import Dependency as Domestic Pipeline Slowly Builds
snippet: EIA data cited by Eagle Nuclear shows U.S.-origin uranium accounted for just 7% of 2025 reactor deliveries — down from 8% in 2024 and a fraction of the domestic share in prior decades — underscoring the strategic vulnerability Washington is trying to close through the Uranium Reserve and new mine approvals. The release notes the domestic pipeline is moving: new projects in Wyoming, Utah, and Saskatchewan are progressing permits, but production timelines extend into 2028-2030 for most.

headline: BANNERMAN APPROVES $353M ETANGO URANIUM MINE IN NAMIBIA — Debt-Free Construction Begins; First Greenfield FID of the Current Nuclear Cycle
snippet: Bannerman Energy (ASX: BMN) and partner CNNC Overseas approved construction of the Etango-8 uranium mine on October 23, committing US$353 million in pre-production capital — funded from existing joint-venture cash of ~US$295 million with no project debt — targeting first yellowcake production in 2028 at ~3.5 million lb U3O8 per year. Industry observers are calling it the first true greenfield uranium mine final investment decision of the current nuclear cycle, with the JV owned 55% Bannerman and 45% CNNC.

headline: RARE EARTH METALS UP 23% IN 2026 — But REMX Mining Stocks Still DOWN 28%; 3.8% ETF Rebound Masks Deepening Decoupling
snippet: The VanEck Rare Earth ETF (REMX) bounced 3.8% this week as critical minerals equities caught a bid, but the ETF still sits 24% below its 2026 high even as rare earth oxide prices have climbed 23% year-to-date — a decoupling that analysts are struggling to explain. The report also notes GM cancelled its supply deal with Vacuumschmelze for a planned U.S. magnet plant, and that Energy Fuels received AUD 126 million in conditional financing from the Australian government for its Donald rare earth project.

headline: GOLDMAN SACHS CALLS U.S. COPPER STOCKPILE 'STRANDED SUPPLY' — Tariff Arbitrage Shipped Metal to COMEX; LME Tightness Remains the Real Story
snippet: Goldman Sachs is pushing back on bearish reads of the US COMEX copper stockpile build, arguing the metal was shipped stateside ahead of threatened tariffs and is effectively stranded rather than available to the global market — leaving LME tightness intact. Chinese Yangshan copper import premiums have hit $183-188 per tonne, close to a 13-year high, lending weight to the Goldman view that the physical market is tighter than headline inventory figures suggest.

headline: AUREKA SHAREHOLDERS GREENLIGHT HIGH GRADE HOLDINGS BUY — Fiddlers Creek Gold Mine and Wedderburn Mill Change Hands October 30
snippet: Aureka (ASX: AKA) shareholders approved the acquisition of High Grade Holdings at a general meeting on October 23, clearing the path for the deal to complete on or around October 30. HGH's assets — the producing Fiddlers Creek gold mine and the Wedderburn gold processing mill in Victoria, Australia — give Aureka an immediate production platform in one of Australia's underexplored gold regions.

headline: AZTEC DRILLS 115.8m OF 0.67 g/t AuEq AT TOMBSTONE, ARIZONA — North Extension Grows 190m West; November Resource Estimate Due
snippet: Aztec Minerals (TSXV: AZT) extended oxide gold-silver mineralization at the North Extension of its Tombstone project in Arizona by up to 190 metres to the west with hole TR26-45, returning 115.8 metres at 0.67 g/t AuEq (0.52 g/t Au and 8.11 g/t Ag). The intercept builds ahead of a maiden Mineral Resource Estimate expected in November 2026, with the total strike length of oxide mineralization now exceeding 1,250 metres.

headline: ALLIED GOLD'S $2,192/oz AISC IN Q2 PUTS HIGH-COST PRODUCERS ON NOTICE — Ethiopian Mine Must Deliver or Margins Evaporate
snippet: Allied Gold reported an all-in sustaining cost of $2,192 per ounce in Q2 2026 — leaving razor-thin margins at current $4,000 gold — but management is betting its Kurmuk mine in Ethiopia, ramping toward 300,000 oz/yr, will transform the cost profile by 2027. The Motley Fool analysis uses Allied Gold as a case study in the structural risk facing high-cost junior and mid-tier producers: when gold retreats to $3,800, companies with $2,200 AISC do not have the operational buffer retail investors may assume.

headline: RAMELIUS RESOURCES LIFTS FY27-30 GOLD PRODUCTION OUTLOOK BY ~5% — GoldSeek SWOT: Australian Mid-Tier Delivers Quiet Operational Beat
snippet: Ramelius Resources (ASX: RMS) raised its four-year production outlook by approximately 5% across FY2027–FY2030, a revision that GoldSeek's Frank Holmes SWOT column highlights as a rare piece of operational good news in a sector dominated by cost-inflation warnings. The upgrade is driven by reserve additions and plant optimisation at its Western Australian operations, positioning Ramelius as a lower-cost alternative to higher-AISC peers during the current gold price consolidation.
